claude.sample_unit: synthetic clinical notes (four simulated patients; 1200 queries per model)

links.outcome: Non-numerical response rate and numeric error across repeated runs and prompt iterations
links.effect: Non-numerical response rate fell from 18.7% to 6.7% (GPT-3.5) and 5.7% to 0.3% (GPT-4); GPT-4 mean error fell from 0.16 to 0.10 points. GPT-3.5 error unchanged (0.42).
links.quote: From initial to final prompt designs, the overall non‐numerical response rate decreased for both LLM models, from 18.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 14.7%–23.5%) to 6.7% (4.4%–10.1%) for GPT‐3.5 and 5.7% (3.6%–8.9%) to 0.3% (0.1%–1.9%) for GPT‐4 ( Figure 2A ).

links.outcome: LLM HEART subscore accuracy against physician gold-standard reference
links.effect: GPT-4 final prompts predicted correct risk group in 100% (96.3%–100%) of calculations versus 81.5% (71.7%–88.4%) for GPT-3.5, judged against blinded physician gold standards.
links.quote: Given the final overall HEART score risk stratification buckets (0‐3, 4–6, or 7–10 points when summing all 5 HEART subscores), 81.5% (71.7%–88.4%) of GPT‐3.5 and 100% (96.3%–100%) of GPT‐4 numerical final HEART score calculations predicted the correct risk group.

links.outcome: Effect of iterative prompt refinement on LLM output validity and accuracy
links.effect: Across three iterations, GPT-4 mean error decreased from 0.16 to 0.10 and non-numerical responses fell for both models; GPT-3.5 mean error stayed at 0.42.
links.quote: For GPT‐4, this same average error decreased from 0.16 (0.11–0.22) to 0.10 (0.07–0.14) points.

unlisted_practices: Iterative prompt engineering framework with quantitative error analysis and stochastic repeat testing

openai.sample_unit: synthetic clinical notes representing 4 simulated patients

links.effect: Final-prompt numerical subscore SD was 0.52 for GPT-3.5 versus 0.33 for GPT-4.
links.quote: GPT‐3.5 had higher variability in its responses, with the mean numerical subscore for the final prompts having a standard deviation of 0.52 for GPT‐3.5 compared to 0.33 for GPT‐4.

links.effect: GPT-4 mean numerical error decreased from 0.16 (0.11–0.22) to 0.10 (0.07–0.14) points.
links.quote: For GPT‐4, this same average error decreased from 0.16 (0.11–0.22) to 0.10 (0.07–0.14) points.
